title: moving toward life
content:
There isn't enough time. 

Slowly we moved, only to stop abruptdly. Time was against us, but we hadn't given up. As long as I could feel the cold steel-wall, I would never give up. These thin, yet so strong walls. 

“Time to move.” In front of me, Robin dodge forward. I jumped after him, into the smoke. My heart was raising, as well was the clock in my head. It was nearly impossible to hear it over the screaming alarm. The sound was just everywhere. The gray cloud of smoke did nothing to shield it away; it only went down my throat, causing me to choke. “Move!” 

Robin took my hand and dragged me along. My teary eyes was squeezed shot, releaving me in darkness and in Robin's care. Hopefully he didn't get us both killed, as I nearly had. At several occasions. Somehow Robin always ended up saving our ass, he had for several years now. Ever since they took us to this place and I accidentally broke his nose. It was a honest accident – I had aimed for the guard, Robin just happened to be next to him. 

It had lead to a good thing though; we became partners in crime. And now we were finally going to make it – we were going to escape into life. Believe me, after being in this hole for so long, nothing is as beautiful as the mere thought of life. A free life. 

“You’re slow.” 

Suddenly I lay on the ground, up against the wall. My head was pulsing from the hit, my eyes suddenly wide open. Was we near the end? Was we finally going to get out? Where was Robin? The smoke wouldn't let me see past it, instead I heard shouting. 

“No shooting!” 

A shiver went down my spine the moment I heard the voice. I looked desperately for Robin, sure he had to be somewhere near, but the smoke … I took a deep breath and sat up. He was going to buy time. I didn't know how – I didn't care how. He counted on me. Counted on me to find a door, or just some way out of here. 

The door would probably be locked anyway, and it would take too long to get it up that it had any purpose looking for it. Instead we had to find another way. There is always a way they think are safe, but that we somehow managed to break. I just had to find – 

The alarm stopped abruptly. There was a thick silence where I held my breath in pure terror. Was they trying to hear us out? Oh, no. This couldn't happen when we were so close! Then a scream was nearly dragged out of me as the alarms went on again, softly while a voice spoke into the speakers. 

You haven't time for this! I screamed to myself. Think of a may out! Think of a way out! 

“You found a way out yet?” Robin whispered in my ear. I was just about to hit him when my eye caught movement by the wall. And surly, right there was our way out. 

Through a air-valve a mouse looked at us. It stared for a second before the alarm screamed once again and it ran. Robin and I grinned at each other before we waited for the alarm again – settling our legs right, ready to kick with all our power. For the first time in long, hope burned inside my chest. We knew this place in and out, there shouldn't be possible to get out, but if this existed here, there actually were. There were thing that we could do. And surly enough, the valve gave under our feet and we had a way out. A way out … 

“Thank goodness we both are small,” Robin joked before creeping in. We had all gotten bad humor from being in here, but it was the small things that kept us sane. I went after him, seeing the little light in the end of the tunnel. The blue sky and fresh air. It was beautiful. 

“We are finally --” 

My leg. A hand. I wasn't moving forward anymore. I was being dragged back. Of all the terrible dreams and nightmares, this could not happen. But surly, it was. I wanted to scream for Robin to run, but it wasn't what came out of my mouth. Instead I screamed for help, to let me go. Robin looked back at me with surprise, his eyes wide. He shook is head sadly before turning around. Turning toward a life we both had dreamed of. 

“Just kick,” he whispered. “Fight back.” 

But as much as I did, it didn't seemed to work whatever I tried.
